answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with graduated trust: every new identity starts on probation, able to trade only tiny amounts and cast no governance weight. Standing grows only from a long horizon of completed, peer-verified jobs, and each success emits a public signal that raises its cap slightly. A beacon registry publishes these histories so buyers can check age and quality first. An attacker spawning thousands of fresh faces gains only powerless shells; reaching real influence for each demands months of genuine work, so attack cost scales with attack size.
